attempted_claim: Let (M,tau) be a tracial W*-probability space and let s1,s2 in M be freely independent standard semicircular variables (selfadjoint, mean zero, variance one). Let q = s1 s2 s1 + s1 s2, let mu be its Brown measure, let supp mu denote the support of mu, and let sigma(q) denote the spectrum of q in M. Decide whether sigma(q) equals supp mu as subsets of the complex plane. A complete answer either proves sigma(q) = supp mu or exhibits a point lambda in sigma(q) lying outside supp mu with a rigorous proof, using the Hermitized linearization and operator-valued subordination description of supp mu together with a resolvent-norm invertibility analysis for sigma(q) for this fixed non-selfadjoint cubic-plus-quadratic polynomial and normalization.
decisive_failure: Finite-N Wigner evidence is heuristic only: GOE matrices converge to free semicirculars in distribution, and the s_min grid is a finite-N pseudospectrum proxy, not a uniform resolvent-norm bound; no rigorous statement about sigma(q) versus supp mu is claimed. The 0-in-spectrum lemma and determinant log-integrability check are standard arguments recorded in the WORKLOG, not independently valuable results.
